title: Twin Screw Pump

introduction.definition: A twin screw pump has two intermeshing screws that do not touch: timing gears outside the pumping chamber transmit the drive and keep the clearances. Cavities formed between the screw flights and the casing move axially from suction to discharge, giving a smooth, non-pulsating flow. External bearings let it handle poor-lubricity and multiphase fluids.
applications: Crude oil and multiphase (oil + gas + water) boosting
Bitumen, heavy fuel and viscous chemicals
key_points: Screws do not touch — timing gears
Handles high gas fractions and solids better than three-screw

classification.configuration: Twin screw, timed, double-suction (double-flow), bearings external

introduction.summary: Two parallel screws with intermeshing threads turn in opposite directions inside a figure-8 housing. External timing gears drive the second screw, so the threads never touch and can handle non-lubricating, viscous, abrasive or gas-laden liquids. In the double-flow arrangement shown, each screw has a left- and a right-handed section: liquid enters at both ends and is conveyed toward the centre outlet, balancing axial thrust. Used for crude oil, bitumen, multiphase production fluids, polymers and food products.

piping: Size the suction line for low velocity (viscous liquids need large suction pipes); provide a strainer.
Fit a pressure-relief valve (integral or in the discharge line) — a positive-displacement pump will build pressure until something breaks if the discharge is blocked.
Support piping independently of the pump.
commissioning: Never start against a closed discharge valve.
Fill the pump with liquid (or ensure the suction is flooded) before start — avoid dry running unless the design allows it.

routine.task: Check bearing temperature and timing-gear oil.

lubrication: External bearings and timing gears oil-lubricated.

video_tutorials.title: Twin Screw Pump — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Twin Screw Pump.
A twin screw pump has two intermeshing screws that do not touch: timing gears outside the pumping chamber transmit the drive and keep the clearances.
Cavities formed between the screw flights and the casing move axially from suction to discharge, giving a smooth, non-pulsating flow.
External bearings let it handle poor-lubricity and multiphase fluids.

Typical applications include crude oil and multiphase (oil + gas + water) boosting; tank-farm and terminal transfer; bitumen, heavy fuel and viscous chemicals; food and hygienic products (sanitary designs).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Pump Casing (Double-Flow), Drive Screw Rotor, Driven Screw Rotor.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Twin Screw Pump works.
Liquid enters at both ends of the double-flow screws.
Sealed cavities between the flights and casing move towards the centre as the screws rotate.
The timing gears drive the second screw and keep the flights from touching.
Liquid leaves at the centre discharge; opposed flows cancel axial thrust.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Twin Screw Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Twin Screw Pump.
Check bearing temperature and timing-gear oil.
Change gearbox oil.
Check screw-to-casing clearances and timing.
Watch for screw rubbing: noise, scoring. Common cause: timing gear wear.
Watch for wear: flow loss. Common cause: abrasives.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
